_comment: LIVE telemetry captured from community SONiC 202505 running on a physical Dell Z9100-ON (service tag SERIAL-B), at idle, via serial console. Companion to z9100-os9-baseline.json (same box under Dell OS9). Captured 2026-08-20.
source: physical Dell Z9100-ON, community SONiC 202505.1196025-ff3c0c9f6, Debian 12
read_via: docker exec pmon sensors  (SMF_Z9100_ON management FPGA)

power_watts._note: Total input 146.7 W corroborates OS9 baseline 143 W idle and the exporter model floor of 145 W.

temperature_c._bcm_u38_note: Tomahawk ASIC on-board sensor; matches OS9-measured die 37 C

fans_rpm._note: 5 fan trays x 2 fans + 2 PSU fans. Higher than OS9 baseline (~6100-6460 RPM) — SONiC default fan policy runs them faster at idle.

FINDING_1_thermal_gap.claim: Thermal telemetry is REAL over SSH/sensors but ABSENT from gNMI (STATE_DB) by default.
FINDING_1_thermal_gap.consequence: thermalctld does not run -> STATE_DB TEMPERATURE_INFO is empty -> 'show platform temperature' returns 'Thermal Not detected' -> nothing to subscribe to over gNMI, even though the FPGA reports 37.7 C on the Tomahawk.
FINDING_1_thermal_gap.fix: set skip_thermalctld:false in pmon_daemon_control.json, restart pmon; thermalctld then populates TEMPERATURE_INFO and a gNMI Get returns it.
FINDING_1_thermal_gap.significance: The gap on the gNMI path is a one-line platform config decision, not a hardware or protocol limit. Shown on real hardware.

VERIFIED_after_fix.action: set skip_thermalctld:false, systemctl restart pmon (backup pmon_daemon_control.json.orig kept on box)
VERIFIED_after_fix.result_state_db: TEMPERATURE_INFO|* keys now present (ASIC On-board Rear, CPU On-board, System Front Left/Right, CPU Core 0-3)

show_platform_temperature._timestamped: 20260820 09:54:00 — live, now readable over gNMI via sonic-gnmi (STATE_DB)

gNMI_proof_over_the_wire._comment: Pulled from the command host to the physical switch (<switch-ip>:8080) via pygnmi, 2026-08-20. Community telemetry runs --noTLS --allow_no_client_auth, so no certs needed. Reproduce: real-hardware/gnmi-probe-hw.py

streaming_subscribe.note: A single pygnmi run of real-hardware/gnmi-probe-hw.py on 2026-08-20 (Subscribe, mode stream, sample @2s). Seen once from the probe and not repeated, so Subscribe is not treated as proven on this hardware.

gNMI_proof_over_the_wire.pfc_ecn: COUNTERS_DB is the same gNMI target; PFC/ECN counters populate once ASIC ports carry traffic (needs the 100G link to switch #2).
